reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that pairwise comparisons of diverse interaction types can be modeled jointly using a modified Bradley-Terry framework. Each interaction type t has an associated valence q_t, representing its informativeness and direction toward dominance. The model introduces a latent stance variable σ_r ∈ {0,1} indicating whether the winner was the instigator (1) or recipient (0). The E-step computes posterior probabilities π_r = λ_{u_r}q_{t_r}/(λ_{u_r}q_{t_r}+λ_{v_r}(1-q_{t_r})), capturing how likely each interaction reflects dominance. The M-step updates q_t = Σ_r δ_{t_r t}π_r/Σ_r δ_{t_r t} and λ_i = Σ_r[π_rδ_{u_r i}+(1-π_r)δ_{v_r i}]/Σ_u A_{iu}/(λ_i+λ_u), allowing simultaneous inference of team strengths and interaction valences. This dual inference enables automatic weighting of play types without manual calibration. The MAP variant adds a logistic prior on s_u, stabilizing estimates and preventing overfitting. The model assumes independence of interactions, no ties, and a single underlying ranking, which may fail in correlated or multi-dimensional settings.
